### Observed differences

- The backbone sequence A45 → A26 → A27 → A28 → A32 is unchanged: each of these pairs co-occurs in all traces in both windows and keeps the same direction in about 98 or more of 100 traces. [REL019, REL022, REL023, REL026, REL028]
- In the earlier window, A45 was followed by A19 (about 35 in 100 of its outgoing transitions), A25 (about 35) or A20 (about 24), and each of the three was in turn followed by A26 (about 92–99 in 100); a direct A45 → A26 transition does not appear in that profile. In the later window, A45 leads directly to A26 in about 94 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, and the ordered pair A45 then A25 within five steps falls from 76 traces to 1 (A45 then A19: from 74 to 1). [DIR045, DIR019, DIR020, DIR025, LAG013, LAG012]
- In the later window, the three alternatives instead attach after A27 or A28: A27 is followed by one of them in about 43 of 100 outgoing transitions (A19 about 16, A20 about 15, A25 about 11) and A28 in about 53 of 100 (about 16, 20 and 17); earlier, A27 led to A28 in about 97 of 100 and A28 to A32 in about 99 of 100, with no transitions to the three in those profiles. The three still always precede A32. [DIR027, DIR028, REL006, REL012, REL017]
- The order between each alternative and A26 flipped: earlier A19, A20 and A25 each ran before A26 (about 36, 24 and 38 of 100 traces); later A26 runs before them (about 31, 37 and 29). Against A28 the later order is mixed (A19 before A28 in about 17 of 100 traces, after it in about 15), indicating two insertion points. [REL003, REL009, REL014, REL005]
- Step distances grew by about one step: A27 → A32 now takes 3 steps in about 93 of 100 traces (2 steps in 97 before); A28 → A32 splits between 1 and 2 steps (about 45 and 54, previously 1 step in 99); A27 → A28 splits between 1 and 2 steps (about 55 and 43, previously 1 step in 98); A45 → A26 now takes 1 step in about 94 of 100 traces (previously 2 steps in 94). [LAG007, LAG010, LAG006, LAG014]
- By event position, A19, A20 and A25 moved from a mean relative position of about one third to about three fifths of the trace, while A26 and A27 shifted slightly earlier (mean 0.35 to 0.33 and 0.58 to 0.56). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- The choice among the three alternatives shifted toward A20: it now runs in about 38 of 100 traces (previously 25), while A19 fell from about 38 to 33 and A25 from about 38 to 30; the three never occur in the same trace in either window. [OCC019, OCC018, OCC024, REL001]
- Smaller shifts elsewhere: A23 and A24 exchange their shares after A21 (A23 down from about 58 to 43 of 100 traces, A24 up from 43 to 58); A17 rises (about 22 to 31) and A18 falls (about 28 to 23) after A16; the repeating region around A43–A49 repeats less (A46 averages 1.75 then 1.53 runs per trace, A47 0.89 then 0.77, A49 0.88 then 0.77, with exits to A50 rising); A39/A40 participation falls (about 47 to 41 of 100) while A41/A42 rises (about 54 to 61 and 60); and after A26 the split between A37 and A38 moves a few points toward A37. [OCC022, OCC023, DIR021, OCC016, OCC017, DIR016, OCC038, OCC039, OCC041, DIR047, DIR049, OCC031, OCC033, OCC034, DIR033, DIR026]
- A few rarely observed activities (A02, A04, A08, A10, A51) show large changes in their successor profiles, but with only about 15–25 observed transitions per window (A51: 6 and 3) these are weak signals. [DIR002, DIR004, DIR008, DIR010, DIR051]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the alternative block A19/A20/A25 — exactly one of which executes per case — is placed later in the later window: earlier it ran between A45 and A26 (A45 → one of the three → A26), whereas later A45 leads directly to A26 and the block is inserted either between A27 and A28 or between A28 and A32, always before A32. This is shown directly and consistently by the successor changes at A45, A19/A20/A25, A27 and A28, by the flipped order relations between each of the three and A26, by the one-step growth of the A27→A28, A27→A32 and A28→A32 distances alongside the one-step shrink of A45→A26, and by the block's event positions moving from about one third to about three fifths of the trace; the core items each exceed about 99 of 100 random re-splits of the same data. Alongside the move, the choice among the three shifted toward A20. [DIR045, DIR019, DIR020, DIR025, DIR027, DIR028, REL003, REL009, REL014, LAG006, LAG007, LAG010, LAG014, POS001, POS002, POS003, OCC019]

Limitations: the evidence shows where the block runs, not why, and it cannot distinguish a relocation of the block from dropping the old branch and adding an equivalent one at the new position, since both produce the same signatures; the smaller shifts in other parts of the process cannot be tied to, or separated from, this change on the evidence given. [DIR045, DIR019, DIR020, DIR025, DIR027, DIR028]

Other differences: the A23/A24 share swap after A21, the A17/A18 shift after A16, the reduced repetition around A43–A49, the A39/A40 versus A41/A42 shift and the small A37/A38 reshuffle after A26 are observed but are not part of the placement hypothesis, and the evidence offers no way to link them to it. [OCC022, OCC023, DIR021, OCC016, OCC017, OCC038, OCC039, OCC041, OCC031, OCC033, DIR026]
